options: As soon as they are addressed and operational at Layer 3
As soon as they are addressed and operational at Layer 2
When they are used as an exit interface
When they are included in a static route
correctAnswers: As soon as they are addressed and operational at Layer 3

questions.question: What characteristic completes the following statement? When an IPv6 static route is configured, it is possible that the same IPv6 link-local address is used for ......
questions.questionHtml:
What characteristic completes the following statement?

When an IPv6 static route is configured, it is possible that the same IPv6 link-local address is used for ......
options: the next-hop address of two different adjacent routers.
a destination host route with a /128 prefix.
correctAnswers: the next-hop address of two different adjacent routers.

questions.question: Consider the following command: ip route 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 10.10.10.2 5 What does the 5 at the end of the command signify?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following command:

 

ip route 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 10.10.10.2 5

 

What does the 5 at the end of the command signify?
options: maximum number of hops to the 192.168.10.0/24 network

questions.question: When would it be more beneficial to use static routing instead of dynamic routing protocols?
questions.questionHtml: When would it be more beneficial to use static routing instead of dynamic routing protocols?
options: on a network where dynamic updates would pose a security risk
on a network that commonly experiences link failures
on a network that has a large amount of redundant paths
on a network that is expected to continually grow in size
correctAnswers: on a network where dynamic updates would pose a security risk

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. How was the host route 2001:DB8:CAFE:4::1/128 installed in the routing table?
questions.questionHtml: Refer to the exhibit. How was the host route 2001:DB8:CAFE:4::1/128 installed in the routing table?
options: The route was manually entered by an administrator.
The route was dynamically created by router R1.
The route was dynamically learned from another router.
The route was automatically installed when an IP address was configured on an active interface.
correctAnswers: The route was manually entered by an administrator.

questions.question: R1 router has a serial connection to the ISP out s0/0/1. R1 router has the 10.0.30.0/24 LAN connected to G0/0. R1 has the 10.0.40.0/24 LAN connected to G0/1. Finally, R1 has the s0/0/0 10.0.50.0/24 network shared with R2. R2 also has the 10.0.60.0/24 LAN connected through G0/0. Refer to the exhibit. The small company shown uses static routing. Users on the R2 LAN have reported a problem with connectivity. What is the issue?
questions.questionHtml:
R1 router has a serial connection to the ISP out s0/0/1. R1 router has the 10.0.30.0/24 LAN connected to G0/0. R1 has the 10.0.40.0/24 LAN connected to G0/1. Finally, R1 has the s0/0/0 10.0.50.0/24 network shared with R2. R2 also has the 10.0.60.0/24 LAN connected through G0/0. 

 

Refer to the exhibit. The small company shown uses static routing. Users on the R2 LAN have reported a problem with connectivity. What is the issue?
options: R1 needs a static route to the R2 LAN.
R2 needs a static route to the Internet.
R1 needs a default route to R2.
R1 and R2 must use a dynamic routing protocol.
correctAnswers: R1 needs a static route to the R2 LAN.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. The routing table for R2 is as follows: Gateway of last resort is not set 10.0.0.0/30 is subnetted, 2 subnets C 10.0.0.0 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0 C 10.0.0.4 is directly connected, Serial0/0/1 192.168.10.0/26 is subnetted, 3 subnets S 192.168.10.0 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0 C 192.168.10.64 is directly connected, FastEthernet0/0 S 192.168.10.128 [1/0] via 10.0.0.6 What will router R2 do with a packet destined for 192.168.10.129?
questions.questionHtml:
Refer to the exhibit. The routing table for R2 is as follows:

 

Gateway of last resort is not set

 

10.0.0.0/30 is subnetted, 2 subnets

C 10.0.0.0 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0

C 10.0.0.4 is directly connected, Serial0/0/1

192.168.10.0/26 is subnetted, 3 subnets

S 192.168.10.0 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0

C 192.168.10.64 is directly connected, FastEthernet0/0

S 192.168.10.128 [1/0] via 10.0.0.6

 

What will router R2 do with a packet destined for 192.168.10.129?
options: send the packet out interface Serial0/0/1
send the packet out interface FastEthernet0/0
send the packet out interface Serial0/0/0
correctAnswers: send the packet out interface Serial0/0/1
